Latest update · 6 November 2026
Whole website now in English: landing page, weight-accuracy report, maintenance report, TPM programme and equipment guide.
Website redesigned: Barabkunda plant photo and BM LP GAS logo, an interactive plant map with the four storage spheres (status of every area), animated figures and charts, and quick search (Ctrl K).

Earlier updates
  • 5 November 2026: New: a world-class TPM programme (8 pillars, maturity 1.4/5, KPIs against world class, a 36-month roadmap) and an illustrated guide to 20 pieces of equipment (NRV, butterfly valve, safety valve, pump, filling head…).
  • 5 November 2026: Maintenance report: 552 SAP orders, total cost Tk 1.08 crore; major-repair risk model (neural network, AUC 0.76); statistical significance and progress.

Safety first

Four things to look at first

Every observation comes from the plant's own records. For review by a qualified engineer.

Decision support, not control

Applicable codes and rules: NFPA 10, 25, 58; LPG Rules 2004; Explosives Act 1884; Fire Prevention and Extinguishing Act 2003.

S1 · Overfilling+48 g on average

Average overfill of 12 kg cylinders in 2026 (to 5 November); highest single cylinder +600 g. An overfilled cylinder has less room for thermal expansion.

NFPA 58; ISO 10691; LPG Rules 2004
S2 · Gas detectors54 months

The last SAP order for gas-detector service is from April 2022; there is no calibration record after it. Only a bump test shows whether a sensor still works.

Manufacturer's calibration interval; NFPA 58
S3 · Spheres and fire protection31-month gap

Fire-extinguisher refill orders once had a 31-month gap; there is no routine test order for the four spheres' PSVs, level gauges and water spray, or for the fire pumps.

NFPA 10; NFPA 25; NFPA 58
S4 · Licences15 kinds

No renewal order for 15 kinds of plant licence after November 2023; for most vehicles the last explosives-licence order is from 2023.

Explosives Act 1884; LPG Rules 2004
